research.title: Causally Sound Memory Invalidation for Long-Horizon Software Engineering Agents
research.description: A framework for detecting and invalidating stale assumptions inside persistent agent memory using causal structure, provenance, and targeted verification.
research.abstract:
Long-horizon software engineering agents accumulate memory across many actions, but those memories are only useful while their assumptions remain valid. This work proposes a causally grounded invalidation model that treats agent memory as a network of claims supported by observations, tools, and derivations.

The framework, CAVI, tracks provenance and dependency structure so that when part of the environment changes, the agent can invalidate only the affected assumptions instead of discarding all memory. This reduces both over-forgetting and dangerous over-trust.
highlights: Separates observation validity, justification validity, and action admissibility.
Uses provenance and transitive dependency closure to find which beliefs became unsafe.
Supports targeted re-verification instead of full memory reset.
Focuses on long-running coding agents where stale assumptions create compounding failures.

research.title: Can Humans Compete with Artificial Intelligence?
research.description: A research essay on task automation, displacement, complementarity, and how work changes when software agents absorb more of the execution layer.
research.abstract:
The question is not whether artificial intelligence will replace all human labor, but which classes of tasks are becoming software-shaped and how that changes the economics of work. This paper examines displacement pressure, productivity gains, and the continuing role of human judgment.

It argues that the most important distinction is not between humans and machines but between work that can be decomposed into repeatable procedures and work that remains socially, strategically, or ethically negotiated.
highlights: Distinguishes automation of tasks from elimination of whole jobs.
Examines complementarity between human oversight and machine execution.
Frames AI as a force multiplier that changes labor composition and bargaining power.
Emphasizes the uneven distribution of gains across industries and roles.
